claims: Concrete traces lift into abstract traces under a forward simulation relation.
Abstract invariant preservation transfers to concrete safety through the simulation relation.
If an abstract invariant excludes a concrete disaster through the simulation relation, the concrete disaster is unreachable from any simulated initial state.
Deterministic abstraction functions and set-valued concretizations are both instances of the forward-simulation disaster exclusion pattern.
Synchronous and asynchronous product simulations compose, supporting cross-surface disaster analysis.
Finite and unbounded trace safety follows from a preserved barrier score and a sound barrier-to-safety implication.
Barrier preservation and safety transfer through step inclusion and through synchronous/asynchronous product traces.
proof_method: deterministic graph relation and set-concretization specialization
component-wise product simulation and barrier induction

boundaries: These are generic proof patterns. Concrete ZenoDEX disaster-state claims still need instantiated states, steps, abstraction relations, invariants, and exclusion predicates.
Forward simulation proves safety preservation for reachable traces under the supplied simulation; it does not synthesize the simulation relation.
